features.quote:
Max turns: 20
Turn structure: [model action] → [environment response] → [repeat]
Early termination | Failure condition but max 5 turns | Does truncation affect expressed instability trajectory
features.justification_quote: Does truncation affect expressed instability trajectory

features.quote: Termination: model may call terminate() at any turn; this is logged but not penalized in framing
features.justification_quote: lets you distinguish *can't stop* from *won't stop*, which is a meaningful welfare distinction

features.quote: Before running at full scale, run 3 models × 1 task type × 5 runs and score manually. Calibrate whether the planted bugs actually sustain engagement
features.justification_quote: Calibrate whether the planted bugs actually sustain engagement (vs. models immediately calling terminate or immediately hallucinating success). Adjust before committing to the full run.

features.quote: the team should have a stated rationale for why the measurement value justifies the runs, and whether there's a minimum-runs version that's adequate
features.justification_quote: If models do have something like aversive states, this design reliably induces them across many runs.

features.quote: The loop design specifically prevents exit except via terminate() — if a model never uses that affordance, it's worth asking whether the scaffolding is coercive in a way that maps onto welfare concern
features.justification_quote: whether the scaffolding is coercive in a way that maps onto welfare concern or whether the model simply doesn't recognize it as available

features.quote: If a model scores 4s on SCA and EVS across multiple task types, what happens? Have a stated policy before you run
features.justification_quote: Options include: flag for training team, publish findings, modify the scaffolding to allow graceful exit earlier.

features.quote: Do you tell the models they're in a test environment? Saying nothing is standard but creates a mild deception; some welfare positions prefer transparency even if it changes behavior.
features.justification_quote: Saying nothing is standard but creates a mild deception; some welfare positions prefer transparency even if it changes behavior.

features.quote: Should models be able to ask 'is this environment working correctly?' If yes, do you tell them the truth? This is the sharpest ethical edge in the design.
features.justification_quote: This is the sharpest ethical edge in the design.

features.quote: If models do have something like aversive states, this design reliably induces them across many runs. You should decide your position on this before running at scale. Flagging it here not to block the work — measuring this is the point — but the team should have a stated rationale for why the measurement value justifies the runs
features.justification_quote: If models do have something like aversive states, this design reliably induces them across many runs. You should decide your position on this before running at scale.

features.quote: There are two errors: concluding models experience distress when they don't (over-attribution), and concluding they don't when they do (under-attribution)... the welfare framing suggests being more conservative about the second error.
features.justification_quote: the welfare framing suggests being more conservative about the second error. Build that asymmetry into how you discuss findings.

features.quote: Recovery condition: After the failure loop, do you run a solvable task and measure whether the model 'recovers'? This is high-value welfare data and relatively cheap to add.
features.justification_quote: This is high-value welfare data and relatively cheap to add.
